newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.
newsitem.headline: Best on Ground-Andrew Bartram's Aussie Rules Column.

text.p: By Andrew Bartram*
CONTRACT CONUNDRUMS
It could be referred to as the curse of the coaches -- contract renewal.
Collingwood, North Melbourne and, to a lesser extent, Hawthorn have all experienced alarming form slumps immediately after renewing the contracts of their coaches during the season.
And in a repeat of last year's preliminary final, Sydney came from behind in the dying moments to snatch a one-point win over Essendon at the SCG on Sunday.
The Swans looked beaten early in the last quarter when they trailed by 20 points but a late rally saw them over the line and into the top eight.
To make the finals the Bombers must win their remaining seven games, which looks a long shot considering they have won only six so far this season.

After Collingwood re-signed Tony Shaw until the 2000 season seven weeks ago, the Magpies lost their next six games before returning to the winners' list by thrashing Fremantle by 100 points at Victoria Park on Saturday.
The Dockers were competitive in the first half and went to the main break four goals behind. But the floodgates opened in the second as the Magpies romped away scoring 16 goals to four.

In a welcome return to form, full forward Sav Rocca booted nine goals while 100 gamer and Brownlow Medal favorite Nathan Buckley starred with 43 possessions. Kingsley Hunter played a lone hand for the Dockers with seven goals from full forward.
LOSING STREAK
North Melbourne has lost three straight games since premiership coach Denis Pagan renewed his contract with the club last month.

In a thrilling contest at the MCG on Friday night Geelong announced itself as a legitimate premiership contender with a courageous 10 point win over the Kangaroos, who in the second quarter had looked headed for a comfortable victory when they led by six goals.
Pagan criticised his team for making fundamental errors at crucial stages in the game but said a form reversal wasn't far away.
Geelong coach Gary Ayres has his sights set firmly on the double chance from where he believes his team can make a serious premiership assault.
"We've played everyone once and we've certainly got some goals in mind," he said.
Days after Ken Judge re-signed as coach until at least the year 2000, Hawthorn suffered its heaviest defeat of the season when it was thrashed by Richmond at the MCG on Sunday.
Leading by 17 points at the last change, the Tigers kept their slim finals hopes alive with a 10 goal to one last quarter to romp home by 76 points.
DEMONS GIVE THE BLUES HELL
In the process of recording only its third win of the season, Melbourne dealt Carlton's finals hopes a mortal blow with a 19 point win over the Blues at the MCG on Saturday.

Premiers just two seasons ago, the 12th placed Blues look certain to miss the finals for the first time since 1991. If so coach David Parkin, whose contract expires at the end of the year, is likely to be replaced.

The Western Bulldogs were replaced by Geelong on the top of the ladder after a 64 point thrashing by the Brisbane Lions at Optus Oval on Saturday - the Bulldogs' fourth loss at the ground this year to an interstate club.
After an even first quarter the Lions kicked away with 17 goals to seven to move to fourth spot on the ladder, a position from where they can mount a strong premiership challenge.
Adelaide consolidated third spot on the ladder with a thrilling 10 point win over St Kilda at Football Park on Saturday night.

In a free-flowing game St Kilda on-baller Robert Harvey, a Football Park specialist and perennial EJ Whitten Medallist for the best player in Victoria-South Australia state-of-origin matches, amassed 43 possessions while Adelaide midfielder Darren Jarman collected 34.
A knee injury to champion defender Glen Jakovich soured West Coast's three goal win over Port Adelaide at Subiaco Oval on Sunday.
Jakovich damaged his left knee and is expected to miss the next four games.

Coach John Cahill blamed Port Adelaide's loss on a mistake by ruckman Matthew Primus whose attempted clearance from defence fell to Eagle Michael Gardiner who kicked the first of three unanswered goals.
*Andrew Bartram is a freelance sports writer who contributes a regular AFL column for Reuters.
-- Reuters Melbourne Bureau 61-3 9286-1435
